title: Market radar & gap tracker for LLM inference features and economics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a living market radar and structured gap tracker to monitor competitive LLM inference capabilities, pricing, and operational features. This tracker will align product, research, and go-to-market teams on where Redwood is ahead, at parity, or behind across: model inference performance (latency, throughput), feature set (function calling, streaming, structured output), cost levers (quantization, batching, KV caching), enterprise controls (VPC, RBAC, audit logs), and pricing/packaging. Deliverables: a searchable dataset, a lightweight dashboard for weekly updates, and an annotated playbook with recommended tactical responses for high-risk gaps.
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated spreadsheet containing canonical data sources (model cards, vendor pricing pages, published benchmarks) for 20+ vendors and 30+ model variants
Dashboard (Tableau/Looker/Notion) that can be filtered by capability, vendor, and date and shows gap status (Ahead/Parity/Behind) for each dimension
A short playbook (1–2 pages) with prescriptive responses for top 5 high-risk gaps (owner, next step, tentative timeline)
Weekly update process defined: who updates, data cadence, and a template for escalation to PM/Eng leadership
tasks: Inventory sources: collect model cards, GitHub repos, benchmark reports, pricing pages (owner: Diego)
Define comparison schema: metric names, normalization rules, confidence scoring (owner: Research lead)
Prototype dashboard with two views: vendor-level and capability heatmap (owner: Product Analyst)
Set update cadence and automation options (scrapers vs manual triage) and estimate engineering effort (owner: Eng PM)
Draft playbook entries for top 5 gaps and circulate for review (owner: Aisha)
comments: 2026-03-01 — Kickoff: aligned on scope with Research, Eng, and Growth. Agreed to prioritize inference economics and enterprise controls first.
2026-03-03 — Research: found inconsistent latency reporting practices across vendors; will adopt a normalized latency-per-token metric and capture measurement methodology in the schema.
2026-03-05 — Eng: flagged potential scraping blockers for vendor pricing pages (dynamic JS). Suggested short-term manual captures + automation backlog ENG-2486.
2026-03-07 — Product Analyst demoed a prototype heatmap in Notion. Early feedback: add a confidence column and source links per cell. Action: prototype v2 with source anchor links.

2026-03-09 — PM review: prioritized 5 high-risk gaps (batching QoS, private deployment latency, streaming SDK parity, per-route cost visibility, model fallback UX). Assigned owners and tentative SLAs in the playbook draft.

2026-03-10 — Decision: canonical datastore will be a locked Google Sheet for now; move to internal DB once schema stabilizes. Next: schedule weekly triage (Fridays 10am PT) and connect Product Analyst with Research for normalization rules.
notes: Assumptions: vendor published numbers are taken at face value but will be tagged with confidence levels.
Trade-offs: manual capture gives speed but increases maintenance cost; automation deferred until schema stable.
Open question: how to align benchmark workloads (sequence lengths, batch sizes) to Redwood production distributions — Research to propose mapping by 2026-03-17.
